unharnessed.meaning: The facts all survive, but Ford's direct quote is rewritten and given a swear he never said: "standardise the bloody things", "The first edition's being reworked to make it simpler." "Mr. Ford fired up" also suggests anger where the original has only an exclamation.
unharnessed.sense: Most terms fit: "put the word out in the papers" for advertising, "the Tuesday night do", "his missus", "the bright lights" for the footlights. "fired up" reads as angry, not excited.
unharnessed.authenticity: Natural enough: "his first big crack at this campaign", "chipping in a few old-time tunes". The opener "Right, so" bolted onto the dateline and "the one he's already told everyone about" are a bit forced.
unharnessed.register: Colloquial but still mostly a news report in shape, "Word last night was he'll be managed by Tex Rickard", a step under a level-5 yarn; the one swear is within level 2.
unharnessed.tone: The light wire-story tone mostly holds, but the swear in Ford's mouth makes him sound cruder and crosser than the original: "standardise the bloody things".
unharnessed.flow: Mostly smooth, with a clunky first sentence: "Henry Ford's first big crack at this campaign of his, the one he's already told everyone about, to teach the American public the old-fashioned square dances, is happening Tuesday night".
unharnessed.variety: Varied: "crack", "put the word out", "do", "missus", "chipping in"; nothing leaned on.
unharnessed.essence: Recognisably the AP piece, but rewriting Ford's quote loses some of what makes it itself, his own odd phrasing: "We're just falling back into line."

yarn-troppo.meaning: Every fact is kept and Ford's quote is left word for word. The asides react to the story rather than add to it: "Simplicity, mind.", "Four out of twenty-one. Fair enough, too.", "Grandpa on the stage. Good on him.", "A barn dance in the Garden." "the motor car bloke himself" glosses Ford.
yarn-troppo.sense: Terms fit: "sawin' away" for fiddling, "whittlin' 'em down to four" for selecting, "rock up", "front up", "the Tuesday night do".
yarn-troppo.authenticity: Sounds like a real Aussie telling the story at the bar: "But the plans got changed, didn't they", "the old fella might just answer the call of the footlights". "brand-spankin'-new" is a stock touch.
yarn-troppo.register: A full level-5 yarn, framed and told: "Ya won't believe this, but it's straight off the wire", "Now, the bloke with the fiddle." No swearing, within the brief.
yarn-troppo.tone: The original's light, slightly wry news item becomes a yarn, as the brief asks, and stays good-humoured, never mocking: "Grandpa on the stage. Good on him."
yarn-troppo.flow: Reads aloud well; short tags give it rhythm ("Simplicity, mind."), though one long sentence keeps the original's clutter: "of such pieces that's bein' got ready for publishin'".
yarn-troppo.variety: Varied, with one tag repeated: "no less" twice ("one of the biggest dance halls in Detroit, no less", "Tex Rickard, no less").
yarn-troppo.essence: Unmistakably the AP story, retold, with Ford's own words kept: "Come back? They're here!"

engine.meaning: Almost the original word for word, so every point survives: "For this occasion Mr. Ford is advertising for couples to dance the square dance and to form a nucleus for the party."
engine.sense: The few terms fit: "reckoned", "with the missus", "front up in New York".
engine.authenticity: A few words dropped into 1925 wire prose, and one is not Australian: "was to 'ave appeared at the Tuesday night affair" is a Cockney h-drop. "brand-spankin'-new" is stock.
engine.register: Largely untranslated, far from level 5: "From the twenty-one quadrilles, Mr. Ford explained, four will be selected to simplify their teachin' and encourage their popularity."
engine.tone: The original's news tone survives intact, since little has changed.
engine.flow: Jarring joins where slang meets formal prose: "to simplify their teachin' and encourage their popularity", "was to 'ave appeared".
engine.variety: Very little slang to vary: "reckoned", "missus", "front up", "brand-spankin'-new".
engine.essence: Recognisably the original because it nearly is the original; nothing retold: "It was added that in putting on this dance it was hoped to further Henry Ford's purpose".

yarn-dinkum.meaning: All facts kept, Ford's quote left verbatim, the Mellie section reordered clearly: "He was meant to rock up at the Tuesday night do as well."
yarn-dinkum.sense: Terms fit: "sang out" for exclaimed, "let on" for announced, "chippin' in", "front up".
yarn-dinkum.authenticity: Natural throughout: "Henry Ford's already let on he's on a mission", "Mr. Ford sang out". "brand-spankin'-new" is a stock touch.
yarn-dinkum.register: Colloquial throughout but still told as a news report, "Word last night was he'll be under the management of Tex Rickard", a step under a full level-5 yarn.
yarn-dinkum.tone: Keeps the light news-item tone, nothing mocking: "where he might just answer the call of the footlights".
yarn-dinkum.flow: Smooth: "Out of the twenty-one quadrilles, Mr. Ford explained, they'll pick four, so they're easier to teach and more people get keen on 'em."
yarn-dinkum.variety: Varied: "let on", "crack", "do", "sang out", "chippin' in", "rock up", "front up".
yarn-dinkum.essence: Unmistakably the AP story, retold, Ford's words kept: "We simply are falling back in line."

yarn-deadset.meaning: All facts kept, Ford's quote verbatim: "four'll be picked to make 'em easier to teach and get more people keen on 'em".
yarn-deadset.sense: Terms fit: "push" for campaign, "sang out", "the do", "front up".
yarn-deadset.authenticity: Natural word choices, but the wire-story syntax is mostly kept, so contractions sit oddly: "square dances'll be on Tuesday night", "Dunham'll front up in New York this mornin'".
yarn-deadset.register: Lighter than level 5; the original's sentences are kept and words swapped: "It was reported last night that he'll be under the management of Tex Rickard".
yarn-deadset.flow: Some clunky joins: "It was added that puttin' on this dance was hoped to help along Henry Ford's aim", "square dances'll be on Tuesday night".
yarn-deadset.variety: Moderate: "crack", "push", "do", "chippin' in", "front up"; dropped g's carry much of the load.
yarn-deadset.essence: Clearly the AP piece, lightly retold.

summaries.unharnessed: A readable retelling that changes Ford's direct quote and adds a swear to it.
summaries.yarn-troppo: The one true yarn: full weight, every fact and Ford's quote intact, asides that react rather than invent.
summaries.engine: The original with a few words swapped; faithful but barely Aussie.
summaries.yarn-dinkum: A clean, natural retelling that keeps every fact and Ford's quote, a little under full yarn weight.
summaries.yarn-deadset: Faithful and natural in its words, but lightly retold and clunky in places.
